html:
"West Getaes" is the map's label, for 700, for the West Geats, the people of Västergötland in what is now southwest Sweden, west of the great lakes Vänern and Vättern.

The Geats were a Germanic people named by writers from Ptolemy to Jordanes, and the hero of Beowulf is a Geat. They lived as farmers and warriors in many small districts with their own assemblies. The West Geats kept their own law, written down in the 1200s as one of the oldest Swedish law books. Their eastern kin were the East Geats, and to the north lay the Swedes. Over the Viking Age the Geats and Swedes came under the same kings; see Swedes and Goths.
